doc/papers/No-Reference Image Quality As.method: All extracted text read; all5 complete pages rendered with Poppler110dpi and visually inspected, including equations1–16, framework diagram, reference thumbnails, tables and scatter plots.

findings: 2009 no-reference quality study combines luminance blur/noise features for perception prediction. It does not establish duplicate identity or a universal best-copy ordering.

Reported training30distorted images and testing207images cover JPEG2000 and white-noise subsets. Correlation with subjective scores is not pairwise keeper-choice accuracy; no HDR/alpha/palette/animation or content-disjoint evaluation established here.

Equations divide by detected edge, blur and noise counts; empty detections and boundary treatment need explicit implementation policy. Narrative neighbor-average blur description differs from printed equation5 based on absolute difference; do not silently resolve this when porting.

Pinned cbird cimgops.cpp295–311 explicitly declares inspiration but substitutes edge/long-edge ratios for the paper blur/noise combination. Paper accuracy therefore cannot validate cbird score. Previously reviewed disabled quality test supplies no independent acceptance.

For our library, quality ranking requires separate qualification after duplicate/pixel/geometry evidence; this paper alone does not justify automatic keeper selection or discarding files. No algorithm port accepted.
